**Proposed mechanism:** GPD1 (HGNC:4377) —PRODUCES→ glycerol-3-phosphate (CHEBI:17700); glycerol-3-phosphate (CHEBI:17700) —LEADS_TO→ glycerophospholipid metabolism (REACT:R-HSA-143511); glycerophospholipid metabolism (REACT:R-HSA-143511) —LEADS_TO→ Congenital generalized lipodystrophy type 1 (MONDO:0012071); AGPAT2 (HGNC:325) —DISRUPTS→ glycerophospholipid metabolism (REACT:R-HSA-143511); glycerophospholipid metabolism (REACT:R-HSA-143511) —LEADS_TO→ Monogenic diabetes of early onset with hearing impairment (MONDO:0012728). Loss-of-function mutations in GPD1 (for MONDO:0012728) impair glycerol-3-phosphate production, disrupting glycerophospholipid metabolism. Similarly, loss-of-function mutations in AGPAT2 (for MONDO:0012071) directly disrupt glycerophospholipid metabolism. Both disruptions converge on the glycerophospholipid metabolism pathway, leading to distinct but related phenotypic consequences.

**How to falsify it:** Demonstration that mutations in GPD1 do not affect glycerol-3-phosphate levels or glycerophospholipid synthesis, or that mutations in AGPAT2 do not impair glycerophospholipid synthesis, would falsify this hypothesis. Additionally, identifying distinct, non-overlapping molecular pathways downstream of these genes that do not converge on glycerophospholipid metabolism would also serve as a falsification condition. _(variant: A common pathogenic variant (AF > 0.001) in GPD1 or AGPAT2 in the gnomAD populations would challenge their sole causal role.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared pathway of glycerophospholipid metabolism could reveal novel therapeutic targets for both monogenic diabetes and lipodystrophy. Interventions aimed at restoring lipid homeostasis or supporting specific branches of this pathway might offer a common therapeutic strategy or inform differential treatment approaches.
